method_card.title: Sine Rule, Cosine Rule & Area Formula
method_card.content:
These tools work in any triangle, not just right-angled ones.

Area = \(\tfrac{1}{2}ab\sin C\) uses two sides and the angle between them.

Sine rule pairs each side with its opposite angle: use it when you know one such pair plus one more side or angle.

Cosine rule covers the rest: two sides and the included angle to find the third side, or all three sides to find an angle. A sine value gives two possible angles between 0° and 180°, so check whether an obtuse answer is wanted.

steps: Gold problems bend the formulas: find an angle from a known area, or spot the ambiguous case where a sine gives two possible angles.
For an area target, rearrange to sinC = 2 × Area ÷ ab. For an ambiguous angle, the obtuse partner is 180° minus the acute one.
New shapes reuse the same idea: a parallelogram is just two triangles.

Keep sin90° = 1 and sin30° = 0.5 in mind; they turn up a lot.

example.question: Find side c when a = 6, b = 10, C = 60°.

gold.hint: Rearrange the area formula: sinC = 2 times area divided by ab, then inverse sine.
gold.display: Two sides of a triangle are 8 cm and 11 cm. The area is 30 cm². Find the included angle to 1 d.p.

guided_steps.say: Work backwards from the area. Area = \(\tfrac{1}{2}ab\sin C\), so sinC = 2 × Area ÷ (a × b). Area = 30, a = 8, b = 11.

misconceptions.message: You may have left out the ½. Area = ½ × a × b × sinC, so sinC = 2 × 30 ÷ 88 = 0.6818 and C ≈ 43.0°. Using 30 ÷ 88 = 0.3409 (no ½) gives the wrong 19.9°.

gold.hint: c squared = a squared plus b squared minus 2ab times cosC, and cos120 is negative.
gold.display: In triangle ABC, \(a = 7\), \(b = 9\), \(C = 120°\). Find \(c\) to 1 d.p.

guided_steps.say: Cosine rule for a side: \(c^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2ab\cos C\). a = 7, b = 9, C = 120°. cos120° = −0.5, and 2ab = 126.

guided_steps.hint: Subtracting a negative adds it on.

guided_steps.done: c ≈ 13.9 cm. The obtuse angle makes c longer than either side, which fits.

misconceptions.message: Check the sign of cos120°. It is −0.5, so −2ab·cosC = −126 × (−0.5) = +63 and c² = 130 + 63 = 193, giving c ≈ 13.9. Treating cos120° as +0.5 gives c² = 67 and the wrong 8.2 cm.

gold.hint: The largest angle is opposite the longest side. Use the cosine rule for an angle.
gold.display: A triangle has sides 5, 6, and 7. Find the largest angle to 1 d.p.

guided_steps.say: The largest angle sits opposite the longest side, which is 7. Call it C. \(\cos C = \frac{a^2 + b^2 - c^2}{2ab}\) with a = 5, b = 6, c = 7, so 2ab = 60.

misconceptions.message: The largest angle is opposite the longest side (7), not the shortest. Using side 7: cosC = 12 ÷ 60 = 0.2, so C ≈ 78.5°. Finding the angle opposite 5 gives 44.4°.

gold.hint: Find the acute angle first, then take it from 180 for the obtuse one.
gold.display: Use the sine rule to find the two possible values of angle B when \(a = 10\), \(b = 14\), \(A = 30°\). Give the obtuse angle to 1 d.p.

guided_steps.say: Sine rule for an angle: sinB = b × sinA ÷ a. a = 10, b = 14, A = 30°, and sin30° = 0.5.

guided_steps.pre: The question wants the OBTUSE angle: 180 − 44.4 =
guided_steps.done: B = 135.6°. Both 44.4° and 135.6° have sine 0.7; here the obtuse one is asked for.

misconceptions.message: That is the acute value. The question asks for the OBTUSE angle: since sinB = 0.7, B = 180 − 44.4 = 135.6°.

gold.hint: A parallelogram is two triangles: work out ab times sinC (no half).
gold.display: A parallelogram has sides 8 cm and 12 cm with an angle of \(65°\) between them. Find its area to 1 d.p.

guided_steps.say: A parallelogram is two identical triangles. Each triangle is \(\tfrac{1}{2}\times 8\times 12\times\sin 65°\). sin65° = 0.9063 (4 d.p.).

guided_steps.done: Area ≈ 87.0 cm², the same as a × b × sinθ.

misconceptions.message: That is the area of ONE triangle (½ × 8 × 12 × sin65°). A parallelogram is two of them, so double it: 8 × 12 × sin65° ≈ 87.0 cm².

bronze.hint: Area is half of the two sides multiplied together, times the sine of the angle between them.
bronze.display: Find the area of a triangle with sides 6 cm and 10 cm and included angle \(30°\).

guided_steps.say: Area of any triangle = \(\tfrac{1}{2}ab\sin C\). Here a = 6, b = 10 and the angle between them is C = 30°.

guided_steps.pre: Halve that (the ½ in the formula): 60 ÷ 2 =
Now multiply by sin30°, which is exactly 0.5: 30 × 0.5 =

misconceptions.message: You may have left out the ½. Area is HALF of a × b × sinC: ½ × 6 × 10 × 0.5 = 15, not 30. Dropping the ½ doubles your answer.

bronze.hint: Use Area = half times a times b times sinC, with sin90 equal to 1.
bronze.display: Find the area of a triangle with sides 8 cm and 6 cm and included angle \(90°\).

guided_steps.say: Area = \(\tfrac{1}{2}ab\sin C\), with a = 8, b = 6, C = 90°.

guided_steps.done: Area = 24 cm². A right angle makes sinC = 1, so the formula is just ½ base × height.

misconceptions.message: That is a × b × sinC without the ½. The area is half of it: ½ × 8 × 6 × sin90° = 24.

bronze.hint: Rearrange the sine rule to b = a times sinB divided by sinA.
bronze.display: In the sine rule, \(\frac{a}{\sin A} = \frac{b}{\sin B}\). If \(a = 10\), \(A = 30°\), \(B = 90°\), find \(b\).

guided_steps.say: Sine rule: \(\frac{b}{\sin B} = \frac{a}{\sin A}\), so b = a × sinB ÷ sinA. Here a = 10, A = 30°, B = 90°, with sin90° = 1 and sin30° = 0.5.

guided_steps.pre: Check the ratios balance: b ÷ sinB = 20 ÷ 1 =
guided_steps.done: and a ÷ sinA = 10 ÷ 0.5 = 20 too, so the sine rule holds.

misconceptions.message: You divided the wrong way. b = a × sinB ÷ sinA = 10 × 1 ÷ 0.5 = 20. Getting 5 means sinA and sinB were swapped.

bronze.hint: Half of 7 times 12, then multiply by sin45.
bronze.display: Find the area of a triangle: sides 7 cm and 12 cm, included angle \(45°\). (to 1 d.p.)

misconceptions.message: That is ½ × 7 × 12 on its own. You still multiply by sin45° (0.7071): ½ × 7 × 12 × 0.7071 ≈ 29.7.

bronze.hint: b = a times sinB divided by sinA.
bronze.display: Using sine rule: \(a = 6\), \(\sin A = 0.5\), \(\sin B = 0.8\). Find \(b\).

guided_steps.say: Sine rule rearranged: b = a × sinB ÷ sinA. a = 6, sinA = 0.5, sinB = 0.8.

guided_steps.done: and b ÷ sinB = 9.6 ÷ 0.8 = 12 too, so it balances.

misconceptions.message: The ratio is upside down. b = a × sinB ÷ sinA = 6 × 0.8 ÷ 0.5 = 9.6. Dividing sinB by sinA the other way gives 3.75.

bronze.hint: Half of 9 times 9, then multiply by sin60.
bronze.display: Find the area of a triangle: sides 9 cm and 9 cm, included angle \(60°\). (to 1 d.p.)

misconceptions.message: That is ½ × 9 × 9, before the angle is used. Multiply by sin60° (0.8660) to finish: ≈ 35.1 cm².

bronze.hint: Work out 25 plus 49 first, then subtract 70 times cos60.

guided_steps.say: You are given \(a^2 = 25 + 49 - 70\cos 60°\). Just work it out. cos60° = 0.5.

guided_steps.done: a² = 39. (You would square-root it for a, but only a² was asked.)

misconceptions.message: You stopped at 25 + 49. The formula still subtracts 70cos60°: 74 − 70 × 0.5 = 74 − 35 = 39.

bronze.hint: Half of 10 times 14, and sin90 is 1.
bronze.display: Find the area of a triangle: sides 10 cm and 14 cm, included angle \(90°\).

guided_steps.say: Area = \(\tfrac{1}{2}ab\sin C\). a = 10, b = 14, C = 90°, and sin90° = 1.

misconceptions.message: That is a × b without the ½. Halve it: ½ × 10 × 14 × sin90° = 70 cm².

silver.hint: b = a times sinB divided by sinA.
silver.display: Use the sine rule: \(A = 40°\), \(B = 75°\), \(a = 8\). Find \(b\) to 1 d.p.

guided_steps.done: b ÷ sinB = 12.0 ÷ 0.9659 = 12.4 too, so the ratios match.

misconceptions.message: The ratio is inverted. b = a × sinB ÷ sinA = 8 × 0.9659 ÷ 0.6428 ≈ 12.0. Dividing the other way gives about 5.3.

silver.hint: c squared = a squared plus b squared minus 2ab times cosC, then square root.
silver.display: Use the cosine rule: \(a = 5\), \(b = 7\), \(C = 50°\). Find \(c\) to 1 d.p.

guided_steps.say: Cosine rule for a side: \(c^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2ab\cos C\). a = 5, b = 7, C = 50°. cos50° = 0.6428 (4 d.p.), and 2ab = 70.

misconceptions.message: You dropped the −2ab·cosC term. c² = 25 + 49 − 70cos50° = 74 − 45.0 = 29.0, so c ≈ 5.4, not √74 ≈ 8.6.

silver.hint: cosA = (b squared plus c squared minus a squared) divided by 2bc, then inverse cosine.
silver.display: Find angle \(A\) when \(a = 10\), \(b = 8\), \(c = 6\). Use the cosine rule. (to 1 d.p.)

guided_steps.say: Cosine rule for an angle: \(\cos A = \frac{b^2 + c^2 - a^2}{2bc}\). Side a is opposite A. a = 10, b = 8, c = 6, so 2bc = 96.

guided_steps.hint: The angle whose cosine is 0 is a right angle.

misconceptions.message: cosA works out as 0, but an angle with cosine 0 is 90°, not 0°. Remember cos0° = 1; it is cos90° that equals 0. So A = 90°.

silver.hint: sinB = b times sinA divided by a, then inverse sine.
silver.display: Use the sine rule to find angle \(B\): \(a = 12\), \(A = 40°\), \(b = 15\). (to 1 d.p.)

guided_steps.say: Sine rule for an angle: sinB = b × sinA ÷ a. a = 12, A = 40°, b = 15. sin40° = 0.6428 (4 d.p.).

misconceptions.message: sinB and a are the wrong way round. sinB = b × sinA ÷ a = 15 × 0.6428 ÷ 12 = 0.804, giving B ≈ 53.5°. Using 12 × sin40° ÷ 15 gives 0.514 and the wrong 30.9°.

silver.hint: Half of 11 times 13, then multiply by sin52.
silver.display: Find the area of triangle with \(a = 11\), \(b = 13\), included angle \(52°\). (to 1 d.p.)

misconceptions.message: That is ½ × 11 × 13 before the angle. Multiply by sin52° (0.7880): ≈ 56.3 cm².

silver.hint: cosC = (a squared plus b squared minus c squared) divided by 2ab, then inverse cosine.
silver.display: Use the cosine rule: \(a = 9\), \(b = 11\), \(c = 14\). Find angle \(C\) to 1 d.p.

guided_steps.say: Cosine rule for an angle: \(\cos C = \frac{a^2 + b^2 - c^2}{2ab}\). Side c is opposite C. a = 9, b = 11, c = 14, so 2ab = 198.

guided_steps.hint: Six over 198 is small and positive.

guided_steps.done: C ≈ 88.3°, just under a right angle.

misconceptions.message: Watch the sign of the top line. a² + b² − c² = 81 + 121 − 196 = +6, not −6. A positive cosine gives an acute angle: C ≈ 88.3°. A minus sign here would wrongly give 91.7°.

silver.hint: a = c times sinA divided by sinC.
silver.display: Use the sine rule: \(A = 35°\), \(C = 80°\), \(c = 10\). Find \(a\) to 1 d.p.

guided_steps.pre: Sense check: A (35°) is the smaller angle, so side a must be shorter than c = 10. Enter a once more:
guided_steps.done: 5.8 is less than 10, so it fits.

misconceptions.message: The ratio is inverted. a = c × sinA ÷ sinC = 10 × 0.5736 ÷ 0.9848 ≈ 5.8. Dividing the other way gives about 17.2.
